_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla, typed out on the slip. Each lesson has two: "start" comes on as the lesson opens, and "check" is a short quiz once the lesson's check is done. Each talk has turns; in each turn Walla Walla says "them" and the player picks one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."). A reply can have a "back" line, and "right": true marks the right answer to a question (it is never scored). Every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Get out this morning’s map from the Bureau and look at the wind arrows. They run along the isobars, round the low, not into it. You’ve been using the rule about your back to the wind. This week, why it works.

replies.say: Why doesn’t the air just fill the low?
replies.back: That’s the question. The answer is under your feet, and it turns once a day.

turns.them: Short one this week. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Air moving north across Washington. Which way does the turning Earth bend it?

replies.say: To its right, towards the east.
replies.back: Right. North of the equator, always to the right.

replies.say: To its left, towards the west.
replies.back: That’s south of the equator. Up here it’s to the right.

replies.say: Not at all, it’s going north.
replies.back: Any direction gets bent, north included. To the right, here.

turns.them: The isobars on tomorrow’s map are packed tight over the Basin. What do you tell the wheat men?

replies.back: Right. Tight lines, steep push, strong wind. Tie down the tarps.
Other way round. Crowded lines mean a strong wind.
Maybe, maybe not. What the crowding tells you for sure is wind.

turns.them: Last one. Why does the wind at the ground slant into a low, when the wind aloft runs along the lines?

replies.say: Friction slows it, so the turn weakens.
replies.back: That’s it. And the air that leaks in has to go up, which is your cloud. Seventy-three.
Not the reason. Friction slows it, the turn weakens, and the push wins a little.
No. Friction slows it, and a slower wind is turned less.
